hero.subtitle: A fall at a Fort Jones store, ranch property, or roadside stop off SR-3 can leave you with injuries and unanswered questions about who's responsible. Our team handles Siskiyou County premises liability claims and can review what happened at no cost.

about.title: Fort Jones Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Fort Jones is a small Siskiyou County community, and many of its everyday spaces — gas stations along Highway 3, shops on Main Street, and small commercial lots — see limited maintenance schedules simply because of the town's size. That doesn't lessen a property owner's duty to fix or warn about hazards they knew about or should have discovered. If you slipped on an unmarked wet floor, tripped over broken pavement, or fell due to poor lighting in a parking area near Rt 3, the property owner or manager may bear responsibility. Building a claim means showing they had notice of the danger and failed to act. That's why documenting the scene — photos of the hazard, witness names, and any surveillance footage from nearby businesses — matters early, before evidence disappears. We don't practice law; we evaluate what happened and explain your options, free of charge.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose Our Team for a Fort Jones Fall

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Evidence
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. We can help gather maintenance records, prior complaints, and photos to build that case.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from a Main Street shop or a Highway 3 gas station is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation can make a real difference.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for a fall, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery reduced by your share of responsibility rather than blocking it entirely.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Fort Jones?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a county building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier formal claim. Speaking with our team soon after the fall helps make sure no deadline is missed.

items.question: What if I fell at a small business and there were no witnesses?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't end a claim — photos of the hazard, your own written account, and footage from nearby cameras can still support your case. Given Fort Jones's small commercial footprint along Main Street and Highway 3, many businesses have some form of surveillance worth checking quickly. Our team can help identify and request that evidence before it's lost.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a consultation?
items.answer: No. Our consultation is free. Attorneys who handle premises liability cases typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
